fact: The Bank of Namibia issued Determination PSD-1 under section 45 of the Payment System Management Act, 2023 (Act 14 of 2023), effective on Gazette publication on 6 January 2026 (Gazette 8822, signed 19 December 2025).
PSD-1 (2026) sets a licensing process for payment services by non-bank financial institutions (paragraph 8) and defines an electronic money issuer as a licensed payment service provider.

Government Notice 251 of 2023 brought the Payment System Management Act, 2023 (Act 14 of 2023) into operation on its Gazette publication, 8 August 2023, with fee regulations for payment service provider licence applications.

The Payment System Management Act 14 of 2023 was promulgated in Gazette 8156 on 28 July 2023 and commenced on 8 August 2023 under Government Notice 251; the Bank of Namibia is the responsible authority.

fact: The Bank of Namibia issued Determination PSD-12 on operational and cybersecurity standards under section 45 of the Payment System Management Act, 2023, effective on Gazette publication on 3 July 2026, replacing the 2022 PSD-12.

The Payments Association of Namibia's 2025 annual report, as reported, says PAN moved from a Management Council to a Management Board during the reporting period in line with the Payment System Management Act, 2023, which treats the Act as operating; the article does not give a commencement date.

The Bank of Namibia issued Determination PSD-10 on fees and charges under section 45 of the Payment System Management Act, 2023 (Act No. 14 of 2023), effective on gazette publication on 24 December 2025 with a six-month grace period for existing providers, and it repeals the earlier PSD-5 and PSD-10 (2020) determinations.

fact: PSD-10, made under the Payment System Management Act, 2023, states that it applies to all payment service providers, defined as banking institutions and non-bank financial institutions, and it binds e-money issuers and providers of e-money wallets and instant payments; new applicants and existing providers are assessed against it.

fact: Bank of Namibia Directive PSDIR-11 of 16 June 2025, under the Payment System Management Act 2023, directs all payment service providers issuing payment instruments to achieve e-money interoperability through the instant payment switch by 26 February 2026.
The Bank of Namibia issued Directive PSDIR-10 under section 44 of the Payment System Management Act, 2023 (Act No. 14 of 2023), effective on signature on 31 March 2025, with contravention an offence.
Directive PSDIR-10 sets the regulator's deadline of 1 April 2027 for payment service providers to execute low-value cross-border Common Monetary Area transfers through the TCIB scheme.
